properties.name: A set of designs that make up one system or system of systems is worked as ONE design graph, though each stays a separate design, often in its own repository
properties.statement:
A set of reflow2 designs that together make up one system or system of systems shall be worked as one design graph: searched, analysed, changed and checked as if they were one. Each design stays a separate design, owned separately and often kept in its own repository or on its own server. This holds at every tier, from the system-of-systems level (integrated-flo over flo2's parts) to the system level (reflow2 used on its own, as Anthony and Alex use it at work).

ANTHONY, 2026-10-07, IN HIS WORDS: "Big picture: I want to treat a set of projects (that are all part of a system or system-of-systems) as 'one' design graph even though they are in separate designs (and probably different repos). Like for instance, in this hub, I'm managing the project at the system of systems level (integrated-flo) for flo2 and at the system level (when reflow2 is not used inside flo2, but by itself like both Alex and myself use at our work places). I think the changes we've made are not contrary to that vision, but I wanted to present the bigger vision and not lose what we're trying to do by focusing too much in individual details."

THE PIECES IT GATHERS, linked DECOMPOSES from each. They are refinements that add specifics rather than a strict 1:1 split; the edge is the closest the vocabulary has for "a facet of this whole":
- req:design-composes (07-25)
- req:recursive-black-box-decomposition (08-07)
- req:a-design-over-the-parts-of-one-thing-holds-what-no-part-owns
- req:one-search-reaches-every-design-a-hub-tracks (09-28)
- req:a-hub-records-each-members-relation-and-a-cross-design-ripple-follows-it (10-06)
- req:a-requirement-reaches-a-design-its-sender-does-not-own-at-proposed-with-its-origin-and-binds-on-the-receivers-word (10-07)
- req:one-design-or-several-is-asked
- req:a-skill-run-in-a-session-holding-several-designs-writes-where-the-fact-belongs (09-22, each fact has one home, at the lowest design that owns it)
- req:a-write-is-warned-when-the-same-thing-already-lives-in-a-related-design (09-22)
The ideas behind them are linked to these already (fact:root-cause-idea-linking-covers-open-ideas-in-pairs-and-a-vision-spread-across-requirements-is-never-gathered-2026-10-07).

WHAT "ONE GRAPH" REQUIRES, AS OF 2026-10-07:
- Know the members and how each relates: built.
- A change's impact crosses designs: built; the agent makes each hop.
- Intent (requirements and decisions) flows down: ruled, planned.
- Status flows up: open idea.
- One question, one answer across all designs: accepted, only search planned.
- Interfaces between members match: mirroring built, barely used.
- The whole holds what no part owns: accepted, unbuilt.
- Each fact has one home: built.

WHERE THE ASSEMBLING HAPPENS: the designs stay separate stores, so "one graph" is assembled at read time. At work, a local reflow2 that can reach every repository or server does it. On flo2.io a hosted design cannot reach another (refused, measured 2026-10-06), but flo2.io holds every hosted design in one process, so it is the natural assembler for integrated-flo. That is recorded as a flo2 idea.

ANTHONY, 2026-10-18, IN HIS WORDS, correcting how the hub had been working: "As graphs at the most basic level are just key:value pairs, my idea was that all key:value pairs for each project could be loaded together and treated as one large set of key:value pairs. Then design is done via this hub level. While we've focused on mathematical proofs and lines of reasoning, some of these may affect other projects and by determining which brainstorm goes to which project, we are assuming that it solely resides in one project. That isn't what I wanted to do by combining multiple graphs into 'one graph'."

HIS CHOICE, the same day: "Write once, link everywhere".
- "Each fact has one home" says only WHERE A RECORD IS STORED and WHOSE WORD CHANGES IT. It never says what the record is about.
- Every write first searches EVERY design and names every design the idea touches.
- It is written ONCE, at the level that covers all of them (the hub level when it is cross-cutting).
- It gets a typed cross-design link to each affected design's records (req:a-relation-between-nodes-in-two-designs-is-recorded-in-the-design-that-makes-it), so it is found from every side.
- Search, impact and reasoning run over the assembled whole.
NOT CHOSEN: "the hub holds all design work" (a member stops being readable alone, and other people's designs cannot work that way); and "one store, no homes" (it would reopen separate ownership and repositories, and leave no clear approver for a shared record).
